title: Guide: MaxSAT, cores
description: A refuted drop set is refined by the core of the failed check: at least one soft clause of the core must be dropped. The abstraction becomes an optimal hitting set of the cores. See the guide page "Implicit hitting sets".

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% Random weighted MaxSAT: 8 variables, 16 soft clauses (weights 1 to 5), 4 hard clauses. Optimum 8.
soft(1,2). pos(1,e).
soft(2,4). pos(2,g). pos(2,h). neg(2,b).
soft(3,4). pos(3,h).
soft(4,2). pos(4,f).
soft(5,1). neg(5,g).
soft(6,4). neg(6,d).
soft(7,4). neg(7,f). neg(7,b).
soft(8,3). neg(8,g).
soft(9,5). neg(9,c).
soft(10,3). neg(10,f).
soft(11,5). neg(11,d). neg(11,c). neg(11,g).
soft(12,5). neg(12,a). pos(12,d). neg(12,b).
soft(13,3). neg(13,b). pos(13,d).
soft(14,2). pos(14,f). pos(14,d). neg(14,h).
soft(15,5). pos(15,c). pos(15,b). pos(15,e).
soft(16,5). pos(16,g). neg(16,e).
hard(h1). neg(h1,h). neg(h1,c).
hard(h2). neg(h2,g).
hard(h3). neg(h3,d). pos(h3,h).
hard(h4). pos(h4,d). neg(h4,e).

% The instance (Instances tab): soft(C,W) is a soft clause C with weight W, hard(C) a hard
% clause; pos(C,V) and neg(C,V) are the literals of clause C.
cl(C) :- soft(C,_).
cl(C) :- hard(C).
var(V) :- pos(_,V).
var(V) :- neg(_,V).
fragments.description: Part of the library example maxsat-ihs.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% The hitting-set solver: which soft clauses to give up (drop). It knows nothing of the
% formula; it only learns the cores, as clauses "drop at least one clause of this core".
{ drop(C) : soft(C,_) }.
% Each call is optimal (A.solve(optimal)): the cheapest set that hits every core so far.
% Its cost is a lower bound on the optimum.
#minimize { W,C : drop(C), soft(C,W) }.
#show drop/1.
fragments.description: Part of the library example maxsat-ihs.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: Part of the library example maxsat-ihs.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% The SAT oracle: an assignment that satisfies the hard clauses and every soft clause that is
% not dropped. It is a witness: if it exists, the hitting set is optimal; if not, the unsat
% core names the soft clauses (assumed not dropped) that cannot all hold.
{ t(V) } :- var(V).
sat(C) :- pos(C,V), t(V).
sat(C) :- neg(C,V), not t(V).
:- hard(C), not sat(C).
:- soft(C,_), not drop(C), not sat(C).
#show t/1.
fragments.description: Part of the library example maxsat-ihs.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# A refuted drop set: its core is a set of soft clauses that cannot all hold.
loop:
    M = A.solve(optimal)
    if not M: stop "the hard clauses are unsatisfiable"
    if C.solve(assume G(M)):
        accept M
        stop
    A.add(G.core(C))
